title: 2014 HMMT February Guts Problem 6
statement: Find all integers \(n\) for which \(\frac{n^{3}+8}{n^{2}-4}\) is an integer.

solutions.text: \(0,1,3,4,6\) We have \(\frac{n^{3}+8}{n^{2}-4}=\frac{(n+2)\left(n^{2}-2 n+4\right)}{(n+2)(n-2)}=\frac{n^{2}-2 n+4}{n-2}\) for all \(n \neq-2\). Then \(\frac{n^{2}-2 n+4}{n-2}=n+\frac{4}{n-2}\), which is an integer if and only if \(\frac{4}{n-2}\) is an integer. This happens when \(n-2=-4,-2,-1,1,2,4\), corresponding to \(n=-2,0,1,3,4,6\), but we have \(n \neq-2\) so the answers are \(0,1,3,4,6\).
